name: Surveyor 3 Lander
goal: To test if the Moon's dust was firm enough to land on and to send pictures back to Earth.
payload: TV camera and a scoop arm for digging soil
story: A robot lander with a TV camera, a scoop arm, and three legs, sent before any astronaut landed.
coolFact: Two Apollo 12 astronauts walked right up to it in 1969 and took its camera and scoop home to study how space affects machines.

name: Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage
goal: To land the first people on the Moon safely and give them a platform to launch home from.
payload: Descent engine, fuel tanks, landing legs, and equipment for the astronauts' moonwalk
story: Eagle was the two-part lander that carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the Moon. The bottom half, the descent stage, stayed behind when they flew home.
coolFact: It is still at Tranquility Base, where humans first set foot on another world.

name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle
goal: To let astronauts travel far from their lander and carry tools and rocks back safely.
payload: Two astronauts, tools, a TV camera, and moon rock samples
story: The Lunar Roving Vehicle: a battery-powered electric car that folded up to fit inside the lander.
coolFact: Apollo 15's crew drove it about 28 km (17 miles). Three of these moon buggies are still parked up there.

name: Viking 1 Lander
goal: To take the first long look at Mars's surface and test the soil for signs of tiny living things.
payload: Cameras, weather station, soil-sampling arm, and life-detection experiments
story: A robot lander that sat in one spot on Mars with cameras, a weather station, and a scoop arm.
coolFact: It worked for over six years, much longer than the 90 days planned, sending thousands of pictures.

name: Sojourner Rover
goal: To test if a small rover could drive on Mars and check what the rocks are made of.
payload: Cameras and an alpha proton X-ray spectrometer for studying rocks
story: The first rover to roll on Mars. It was about the size of a microwave oven.
coolFact: It was built to work for 7 days but kept going for about 3 months!

name: Spirit Rover
goal: To look for clues that Mars once had water, by studying rocks and soil.
payload: Panoramic camera, rock-grinding tool, and science instruments on its arm
story: A golf-cart-sized rover with cameras, a rock-grinding tool, and science instruments on its arm.
coolFact: Planned for 90 days, it worked for about 6 years. Its wheels dug up bright soil that hinted at hot water long ago.

name: Opportunity Rover
goal: To hunt for signs that water once flowed on Mars and might have helped life start.
payload: Panoramic camera, rock-grinding tool, and science instruments on its arm
story: Spirit's twin rover. It landed on the other side of Mars.
coolFact: It was planned for 90 days and lasted almost 15 years, driving about 45 km, farther than a marathon!
